blocks.content: METEOR is a core topic in AI Safety & Evaluation. It helps engineers measure whether an AI system is useful, correct, safe, fair, and stable for its intended users.
This chapter develops METEOR from first principles through implementation, tradeoffs, production risks, observability, and interview reasoning. It belongs to the Generation Metrics module.

blocks.title: Topic-specific mental model
blocks.content: A metric is a proxy for one quality dimension. Document what it rewards, what it misses, and how it correlates with human judgment.
1. What METEOR Means
METEOR should be defined by the problem it solves and the contract it offers. A strong implementation makes assumptions explicit instead of hiding them inside framework defaults or a notebook.

blocks.content: The interview-quality explanation of METEOR connects the concept to a concrete problem, a working design, and its tradeoffs.
2. End-to-End Engineering Flow
A production implementation of METEOR is not an isolated function. It participates in a complete flow with validation, state, execution, and feedback.

["Define the behavior and risk being measured.","Create representative cases and slices.","Choose deterministic, model-based, and human evaluators.","Run baselines and candidate versions.","Analyze failures by category and severity.","Gate releases and monitor production drift."]
items: Define the behavior and risk being measured.
Create representative cases and slices.
Choose deterministic, model-based, and human evaluators.
Run baselines and candidate versions.
Analyze failures by category and severity.
Gate releases and monitor production drift.

blocks.title: Boundary rule
blocks.content: Validate data when it crosses a boundary. Never assume a model, library, user, file, tool, or remote service returned a trusted value.
3. Implementation Pattern

for case in evaluation_set:
    output = system.run(case.input)
    result = evaluator.score(output, expected=case.expected, rubric=case.rubric)
    report.record(case.id, result, slice=case.slice)
release_gate.assert_thresholds(report)

blocks.content: The pattern keeps METEOR behind a narrow interface. Business logic depends on that interface, while frameworks, providers, storage, and infrastructure remain adapters that can be tested or replaced.

blocks.content: 4. Correctness and Evaluation
Correctness for METEOR needs a task-specific evaluation set. Include ordinary cases, boundary cases, realistic failures, and slices that could be hidden by a single average.
["Measure task success and correctness.","Measure groundedness and hallucination rate.","Measure safety violation rate.","Measure slice-level fairness.","Measure latency and cost."]
items: Measure task success and correctness.
Measure groundedness and hallucination rate.
Measure safety violation rate.
Measure slice-level fairness.
Measure latency and cost.

blocks.title: Debugging order
blocks.content: Reproduce the input, verify preprocessing, inspect intermediate state, validate configuration and version, isolate the failing dependency, then compare against a known baseline.
6. Production Design

{"headers":["Concern","Production requirement"],"rows":[["Reliability","Timeouts, bounded retries, idempotency, fallback, recovery"],["Security","Least privilege, validation, isolation, secret hygiene"],["Observability","Structured logs, traces, metrics, version metadata"],["Scalability","Backpressure, batching, caching, horizontal limits"],["Cost","Budgets, usage attribution, capacity and provider controls"]]}
METEOR is ready for production only when operators can detect failure, understand why it happened, contain its impact, and restore service without guessing.

["Define METEOR in one clear sentence.","Explain the problem, baseline, and key abstraction.","Draw the end-to-end data or request flow.","Name the most important correctness and failure cases.","Discuss one quality, latency, cost, and security tradeoff.","Describe evaluation and production monitoring.","Explain how the design changes at ten times the scale."]

blocks.title: Key takeaways
points: METEOR is a system capability, not an isolated API call.
Explicit contracts and evaluation make the implementation trustworthy.
Production quality comes from bounded behavior, observability, and recovery.
